title: Midday kernel sketchpad — bug triage + perf TODOs
content:
Midday kernel sketchpad — quick triage + perf ideas (Ashok)

Date: 2026-03-11 (notes captured across the day)
Context: after the 2026-03-10 deploy (canary -> prod) we saw intermittent p95 spikes on short-context text-gen paths. This is my working scratchpad for triage, lightweight repros, and small experiment ideas. Not polished — notes to self.

Observed symptoms
- p50 stable (~35ms), p95 moved from ~70ms to 140–220ms for short prompts (len < 64 tokens) on model:gpt-medium-quant.
- spikes correlate with sustained traffic bursts from customer X (route: /v1/completions, model pinned).
- stack traces around spike windows show more frequent kernel page faults in the C++ allocator and increased KV cache misses.
- SRE reported OOM kill on one Dedicated node yesterday (node-06) — probably unrelated but keep in mind.

Quick repro attempt (local dev)
1) simulate 200 qps with variable prompt lengths (50% <64, 30% 64-256, 20% >256).
2) run on metal-rt-small (local) with same model binary as prod (built 2026-03-09).
3) capture kernel logs, perf top, and /proc/vmstat every 10s.

Initial hypotheses
- KV cache eviction policy changed subtly in kernel commit (ref PR 1427) — causing higher thrashing for small sequences.
- Quantized kernel path picks a different allocator path which increases page faults under sustained small-batch load.
- Autoscaler burst behavior increases concurrent worker count, which increases aggregate working set beyond node memory and triggers page reclaim.

Immediate triage checklist (priority order)
- [ ] Reproduce locally with payload generator (use load-generator branch: loadgen/kv-evict-test).
- [ ] Run perf record on minority of canary hosts (2 nodes) during next traffic window.
- [ ] Add short-term metric: kv_cache_local_hit_rate (per-worker) to the telemetry exposed by runtime.
- [ ] Check allocator flags in the 2026-03-09 build vs previous stable (2026-03-02).
- [ ] Rollback PR 1427 on a single canary pool if repro is straightforward.

Notes on KV cache behavior
- Current policy: global LRU across shards, eviction when free_pages < threshold. Suspect threshold too low when many small requests produce many short-lived KV entries.
- Idea: add a small-time bucketed TTL for entries created by sequences < 64 tokens — cheap heuristic: lifecycle <= 2s. This could cut churn for small prompts.
- Short-term patch: lower kv_shard_count for canary to reduce cross-shard contention (experimental).

Perf micro-experiments to run (low-risk)
- Experiment A: set KV eviction threshold +20% and observe p95 for 30m.
- Experiment B: enable async prefetches only for large sequences (>128) and disable for small. Measure CPU overhead.
- Experiment C: replace jemalloc arena behavior to use per-thread caches for small allocs (build with MALLOC_CONF override).

Debug artifacts to collect
- perf record/collate for hotspots in runtime::kv::Lookup and runtime::alloc::*
- /proc/vmstat and vm.swappiness snapshot across spike windows
- dmesg logs for page faults and OOM killer activity
- runtime debug dump: kv_shard_stats, live_allocations_count, kv_prefix_hit_histogram

Tickets and ownership
- INF-3245: "p95 spikes after 2026-03-10 deploy" — assigned to me (Ashok) as lead.
- INF-3251: "node OOM investigation" — SRE (Diego) owns. Keep coordinated.
- GH-1427: allocator change (author: Mina) — suspect but need repro.

Quick action plan (next 48h)
Day 0 (today):
- repro locally with loadgen (2h) + collect perf (1h) -> update INF-3245 with attached flamegraphs.
- add simple kv_cache_local_hit_rate metric (quick change in telemetry lib) -> deploy to canary (2h).

Day 1:
- Run controlled canary with small-batch bias traffic (6h ramp).
- If p95 still high, rollback GH-1427 on one canary pool and compare.
- If rollback reduces p95, schedule full rollback and postmortem.

Day 2:
- If regression remains, try TTL heuristic for small sequences or lower shard_count.
- Plan longer-term fix: revisit allocator paths and consider per-worker KV partitioning.

Notes to self / random thoughts
- We might be overfitting to short prompts. Some customers do only short prompts and they are sensitive to head-latency — consider a per-route config for kv_behavior.
- Add an e2e eval that sends 90% short prompts and tracks p50/p95 token-latency per commit. Automate as a pre-merge check for runtime changes.
- Remember to ping @Mina in Slack before rolling back her PR — avoid surprise.

Snippets / CLI commands
- repro load (local): ./dev/loadgen --rate 200 --short-bias 0.6 --model gpt-medium-quant --out /tmp/load-logs
- collect perf: sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- ./bin/runtime --config canary.yaml; sudo perf script > perf-unfolded.txt; flamegraph.pl perf-unfolded.txt > f.svg
- quick telemetry grep: curl -s localhost:9090/metrics | grep kv_cache_local_hit_rate

Open questions
- Did the allocator change affect only certain hardware (A100 vs H100 micro-behaviors)? Need to tag by hardware when collecting data.
- Are the affected requests always single-tenant? Could be customer-specific request pattern that stresses eviction.
- Is there any interaction with the new batching heuristics deployed last month?

References / links
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1427
- Jira: INF-3245
- Slack thread: #runtime-kernel (thread ts=1710273842.000500)

Next immediate steps (right now)
- start local repro (30m)
- add kv metric change to telemetry branch and open small PR targeting canary (45m)
- message Mina + Diego with current notes and plan (15m)

-- end scratchpad --

(If I'm stepping away: leave loadgen running, drop log tarball at /tmp/ashok-kv-investigation.tar.gz, ping me on Slack if perf traces look noisy)
